slice: The Apps panel's browser address bar searches, not just navigates
method: desktop patch 0021 change + CDP on the running Agents window + bun test + bun run typecheck

problem.symptom: typing words into the Apps panel's browser box did nothing useful
problem.detail: normaliseUrl prefixed `https://` to anything without a scheme, so a search term became the host `https://cats and dogs` and the page failed to load - while the field's own placeholder already read 'Search or enter URL'

change.rule: a value with a scheme (https:, file:, mailto:) is used as typed; a single token that looks like a host - localhost, an IPv4 address, or a dotted name with a two-letter-or-longer suffix, each with an optional port and path - is opened over https; anything else goes to the search engine
change.engine: https://www.google.com/search?q= (the search box's placeholder and the reference browser's engine), with the term percent-encoded

verified.search: CDP on the running window: opening the Apps panel's Browser tab and typing 'cats and dogs' then Enter produced a page target titled 'cats and dogs - Google Search (the engine's localised title)' at https://www.google.com/search?q=cats%20and%20dogs
verified.url: typing 'example.com' then Enter produced the 'Example Domain' page at https://example.com/ - a bare host is still a URL, not a search
verified.unitTests: apps/macos/test/ide-native-workbench.test.ts pins the search endpoint and the encoded-term return in the 0021 patch text, alongside the address bar it belongs to
verified.patchAgreement: 0021 regenerated for its own file only, digest updated, 24/24 patches apply from the pinned base and the produced tree equals the checkout
verified.suites: 721 pass / 0 fail across packages/omp-adapter, packages/relay, apps/host and apps/macos/test

notVerified: The engine's own rendering: the search page loaded and reported its title, but nothing beyond the navigation was inspected.
Which engine a user would prefer: Google is hard-coded here, matching the placeholder, with no setting to change it.
A host whose suffix is not a real TLD (e.g. 'readme.md') is treated as a URL and will fail to load rather than being searched; the rule is deliberately simple rather than carrying a TLD list.
